transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

NO. Do not try to use the oven again.

This is a potentially dangerous situation. The symptoms you described—delayed ignition followed by a loud "WHOOPH" (a small explosion) and a strong gas smell—are classic signs of a gas accumulation issue. This means gas was building up in the oven cavity before it finally ignited, which can cause damage to the oven and pose a serious fire or explosion risk.

### 🚨 IMMEDIATE ACTION STEPS:

1.  DO NOT TURN ANY ELECTRICAL SWITCHES ON OR OFF.
• Do not turn on lights, exhaust fans, or any other appliances. A spark from a switch can ignite residual gas in the air.
2.  VENTILATE THE AREA SAFELY:
• Open windows and exterior doors to let fresh air in.
• If you have an internal door leading away from the kitchen, close it to contain the gas spread while you ventilate.
3.  SHUT OFF THE GAS SUPPLY (if safe to do so):
• Locate your gas emergency shut-off valve (usually near the gas meter or where the pipe enters your home). Turn it off if you know how and can reach it safely without creating a spark.
4.  EVACUATE:
• Leave the house immediately with all occupants and pets.
5.  CALL FOR HELP FROM A SAFE LOCATION:
• Once outside, call your local gas emergency line (e.g., National Gas Emergency Service in the UK: 0800 111 999; Gas Safe Register for a repair engineer).
• If you smell gas strongly throughout the house or feel dizzy/nauseous, also consider calling the fire department.

### Why this happened:
• The "delayed lighting" suggests a problem with the igniter (it may be weak or failing) or a blockage in the gas jets.
• The "WHOOPH" indicates that enough gas had accumulated to create a flammable mixture before ignition occurred. This is known as a delayed ignition or backfire.
• The strong smell afterwards means there are likely leaks, damaged seals, or residual gas trapped in the oven cavity.

### What to do next:
• Do not attempt to reset or restart the oven.
• Only a qualified Gas Safe registered engineer (or equivalent certified technician in your country) should inspect and repair this.
• Explain exactly what happened: "Delayed ignition followed by a loud pop and strong gas smell."

Your safety is the priority. Please treat this as an emergency and get professional help immediately.
